title: Telegram Caps Bots at 20MB. My Pipeline Takes 2GB | vitalii.no
description:
How swapping the Bot API for a full MTProto client removed the ceiling that was silently dropping the biggest stories from my news pipeline.

The Telegram Bot API refuses to download anything over 20MB. My aggregation pipeline pulls from 6 Telegram channels, and news video is routinely 50 to 200MB, sometimes past 500MB for the reports that matter most. Every one of those simply failed to ingest. The bigger the story, the more likely it was the one that never arrived.

The fix was to stop being a bot. A Deno service built on MTKruto connects as a full MTProto client — the same protocol a real Telegram app speaks — which lifts the download ceiling to 2GB. From there processAndUploadVideo takes over: the file goes to YouTube as an unlisted upload through Data API v3 for embedding on the site, and the whole job runs inside GitHub Actions so nothing heavy touches the serverless backend.

Every 'video too large' failure is gone — 100 percent of them. The pipeline now ingests anything from a 50MB clip to a multi-gigabyte documentary. Speaking MTProto also opened up channel metadata and full message history that the Bot API never exposed.
